candidates.title: Commission opens targeted consultation on copyright challenges, including use of protected content in AI
candidates.summary: On 29 September 2026 the European Commission's digital-strategy site announced a targeted consultation (online survey) on challenges and the way forward in the area of the effect of technology on copyright. It builds on a call for evidence held earlier in 2026. The page lists four areas, the first being the use of copyright-protected content in artificial intelligence; the others are the fight against online piracy of content like live events, the application of the single equitable remuneration right of music performers and producers, and copyright of scientific research. It names generative AI providers and other actors in the AI value chain among those invited to respond. The page states the consultation remains open until 3 November 2026. The EUSurvey questionnaire was opened and its title and topics (including generative AI and copyright) were read, but its questions were not reviewed in full.
candidates.why_it_matters: Responses may inform whether the Commission proposes changes to the EU copyright framework as it applies to the use of copyright-protected content in AI. Developers of generative AI models and rightholders can submit views until the stated deadline.
